doc_title: Temperature creep in hot water recirculation
cause_text: Recirculation flow too low to satisfy the master mixing valve's minimum flow requirement
check_text: Confirm loop flow meets the mixing valve's minimum GPM and watch outlet temperature overnight when nothing is drawn
expected_obs: Loop flow below the valve minimum; mixed outlet temperature creeps up or droops at night
action: Use a correctly sized, constantly running recirculation pump so the valve minimum flow is always met
anchor: enough flow to meet the valve minimum flow

doc_title: Temperature creep in hot water recirculation
locator: Article body, second listed requirement (valve close-off)
cause_text: Master mixing valve does not fully close its hot inlet, so hot water leaks through when nothing is drawn
check_text: Watch the mixed outlet temperature overnight while no fixture is drawing
expected_obs: Outlet temperature drifts above (creep) or below (droop) the valve setting during no-draw periods
action: Pipe bridge and return balancing valves as in the schematic, or use a valve with 100 percent hot close-off
anchor: 100% close-off on it's inlet ports

doc_title: Temperature creep in hot water recirculation
locator: Article body, third listed requirement (return/bypass valves)
cause_text: Wrong split of recirculated water between returning to the storage tank and returning to the mixing valve cold side
check_text: Watch outlet temperature at night with no fixture draw after adjusting the bypass valve
expected_obs: Too much return to the tank gives creep (outlet too warm); too little gives droop (outlet too cool)
action: Open the bypass valve to the tank only slightly; the return valve is normally left fully open
anchor: Too much water going back to the storage

locator: Section: Point-of-distribution temperature protection (bridge and return valves)
cause_text: No recirculated flow returning to the water heater, so the loop is not carrying heat to the mixing valve
check_text: Compare mixed supply temperature leaving the point-of-distribution mixing valve with its setting
expected_obs: Supply temperature leaving the mixing valve is lower than the valve setting
action: With no draw, slowly open the bridge valve until outlet temperature stabilizes; partly close the return valve if needed
anchor: will likely be lower than the setting

cause_text: Long or uninsulated recirculation loop loses far more heat, so the flow needed to hold temperature rises
expected_obs: Heat-loss rate substantially higher than for an insulated loop; insulation lowers heat loss and the required recirculation flow
action: Insulate the loop piping, which reduces heat loss and the recirculation flow needed
anchor: If the loop is long and uninsulated

locator: Section: Recirculation flow rate (allowed temperature drop)
cause_text: Recirculation flow set for a large temperature drop along the loop, leaving the farthest fixture below acceptable temperature
check_text: Compare the temperature drop from heat source to farthest fixture (supply minus return) with the 5 to 10 F design drop
expected_obs: Loop temperature drop larger than the suggested 5 to 10 F; farthest-fixture water below the acceptable supply temperature
action: Design for a smaller allowed drop, which needs more recirculation flow
anchor: acceptable supply temperature at the farthest fixture

cause_text: A branch with low recirculation flow because the multi-branch loop is not balanced
check_text: Read flow through each branch balancing valve (manometer across a fixed-orifice valve, or direct-reading valve) against design
expected_obs: Low-flow branch cannot deliver adequate hot supply temperature at its farthest fixtures
action: Balance each branch so flow is adequate but not excessive
anchor: Branches with low recirculation rates could fail

cause_text: Without balancing, branches near the circulator take more flow than branches farther away
check_text: Compare per-branch flow readings from the balancing valves against design flow
expected_obs: Distant branches show lower recirculation flow than nearer branches
action: Fit and set a balancing valve on each return branch
anchor: higher recirculation flow rates compared to branches that

cause_text: Adjusting one manual balancing valve shifts flow in the other branches, so a recent adjustment can upset other branches
expected_obs: Flow in other branches changes after one valve is adjusted
action: Re-adjust each valve iteratively several times until all branches are balanced
anchor: changes the flow rates through the other branches

cause_text: Built-in heater thermostats give imprecise control of leaving water temperature
expected_obs: Leaving-heater temperature not tightly held to the setting
action: Do not rely on tank controls alone to regulate delivery temperature; add a mixing valve
anchor: do not provide precise control of the water

locator: Section on Legionella control by raising heater temperature (scald risk)
cause_text: Heater thermostat raised for Legionella control without temperature-limiting devices at fixtures
expected_obs: Scalding-hot water delivered at fixtures such as lavatory faucets
action: Install suitable temperature-limiting devices (mixing valves) when raising heater temperature
anchor: without installation of suitable temperature-limiting devices

locator: Heat exchanger scaling and fouling discussion
cause_text: Hard domestic water scales the heat exchanger and fouling degrades its performance
expected_obs: Reduced heat transfer; exchanger must be kept with little if any fouling for reliable performance
action: Maintain the exchanger, including chemical cleaning; replace if scaling is beyond what cleaning corrects
anchor: Hard domestic water will scale any heat exchanger

cause_text: Inadequate flow through the heat exchanger limits heat transfer; boilers reach high limit and short cycle
expected_obs: Heat transfer limited; boilers hit high-limit settings and short cycle
action: Provide the required primary flow with a correctly sized pump and piping
anchor: Flow bottlenecks cause heat transfer bottlenecks

cause_text: Pressure reducing valve or backflow preventer closes the system, so heated water has nowhere to expand and pressure rises
expected_obs: System pressure climbs during no-flow periods while water is heated
action: Add a potable-rated expansion tank or a pressure-relief expansion device on the heater supply
anchor: reducing valves, backflow preventers, and other one-way valves

cause_text: Thermal expansion overpressure in a closed heater system
check_text: Install a pressure gauge that records the pressure rise through heating cycles
expected_obs: Pressure rises above supply pressure while the heater is heating, confirming thermal expansion
action: Install an expansion tank designed for potable water
anchor: confirmed using a Watts IWTG gauge

cause_text: Thermal expansion pressure rise relieved through the T&P valve

expected_obs: Small recurring discharges from the T&P valve
action: Address the thermal expansion with an expansion tank so the T&P valve is not used for expansion
anchor: small, recurring discharges from the T&P valve

locator: Section: What You Need to Know
cause_text: Heater temperature or pressure at an unsafe level (not thermal expansion alone)
check_text: Look for any discharge from the T&P valve in normal operation
expected_obs: Any water discharge from the T&P valve; none is expected in normal operation
action: Have a qualified service technician or licensed plumber investigate promptly
anchor: may indicate an unsafe temperature or pressure condition

cause_text: Missing or failed check valves at mixing-valve inlets let hot water thermosiphon into the cold supply
expected_obs: Hot water flows toward the cold supply when check valves are absent and differential pressure is extreme

doc_title: CircuitSolver Thermostatic Balancing Valve, Domestic Hot Water System
cause_text: Branches are balanced only with static manual valves; flow follows the path of least resistance, which keeps changing with use
expected_obs: Some branches go cold or imbalanced as the path of least resistance shifts
action: Use thermostatic balancing valves at the end of each branch instead of manual flow valves
anchor: Water flows to the path of least resistance.

doc_title: Domestic hot water recirculation (DHWR) sizing app (V 1.0)
cause_text: Circulator too small to move enough flow to keep water in the lines hot
expected_obs: Recirculation system does not keep lines hot as intended
action: Size the circulator to the loop head loss and heat loss rather than guessing
anchor: An undersized circulator might not provide enough flow

doc_title: Domestic hot water recirculation (DHWR) sizing app (V 1.0)
cause_text: Circulator too large, causing excess flow, higher energy use and wear on the piping
expected_obs: Excess flow leading to premature pipe wear and failures
action: Do not oversize the circulator; limit return-line velocity
anchor: premature pipe failures due to wear and tear

cause_text: No circulation during idle periods, so water standing in the pipes cools and must be flushed out before hot arrives
check_text: Measure how long hot water takes to arrive at the fixture after opening the tap
expected_obs: Long wait while cooled water is cleared from the pipes
action: Keep domestic hot water circulating back to the heater at a minimum temperature
anchor: relatively long time to remove this cool water

cause_text: Air in the recirculation system keeps it from functioning (air-bound pump or loop)

locator: Section on circulation flow and heat loss

cause_text: Insulation and pipework routing strongly affect the heat load the circulation loop must replace

action: Insulate piping and route it to limit unwanted heat transfer
anchor: decisive influence on the effective heat loads

doc_title: Hydraulic balancing for hot water (Hycleen Balance)
cause_text: Hot water circulation not hydraulically balanced, especially in larger systems
expected_obs: Volume flows not matched across circuits; pump needs more power when balanced flows are not set
action: Hydraulically balance the volume flows, for example with temperature-controlled balancing valves
anchor: essential for ensuring a well-functioning hot water circulation

cause_text: Risers not held at a set temperature end up insufficiently heated
expected_obs: Some risers insufficiently heated; hot water not equally fast at all fixtures
